def bar_labels(ax, fmt="{:,.0f}", pad=3):
    for c in ax.containers:
        ax.bar_label(c, labels=[fmt.format(v) if v else "" for v in c.datavalues], padding=pad,
                     color=INK_2, fontsize=8)


def plot_sales(code):
    s = sales[sales["series"] == code].set_index("market_code").loc[MARKET_ORDER]
    years = ["volume_2024", "volume_2025", "volume_2030"]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.2))
    x = np.arange(len(MARKET_ORDER))
    for i, (y, a) in enumerate(zip(years, [0.35, 0.6, 1.0])):
        ax.bar(x + (i - 1) * 0.27, s[y], width=0.25, color=SERIES[code]["color"], alpha=a,
               label=y.split("_")[1] + (" (plan)" if y.endswith("2030") else ""), edgecolor="white", linewidth=1)
    ax.set_xticks(x, MARKET_ORDER)
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(lambda v, _: f"{v / 1000:.0f}k")
    ax.set_title(f"{SERIES[code]['name']} ({code}) — units by market")
    ax.legend(ncol=3, loc="upper right")
    ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
    bar_labels(ax, "{:,.0f}")
    plt.show()
    out = s[years + ["growth_25_30"]].copy()
    out.loc["Total"] = [*s[years].sum(), s["volume_2030"].sum() / s["volume_2025"].sum() - 1]
    out["share_2025"] = out["volume_2025"] / s["volume_2025"].sum()
    return out.style.format({"volume_2024": "{:,.0f}", "volume_2025": "{:,.0f}", "volume_2030": "{:,.0f}",
                             "growth_25_30": "{:+.0%}", "share_2025": "{:.0%}"})


def feedback_profile(code):
    f = feedbacks[feedbacks["series"] == code]
    n = len(f)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 3.2))
    for ax, col, title in zip(axes, ["Country", "Source", "powertrain"], ["Country", "Source", "Powertrain"]):
        vc = f[col].value_counts()
        if col == "Country" and len(vc) > 6:
            vc = pd.concat([vc.iloc[:6], pd.Series({"other": vc.iloc[6:].sum()})])
        ax.barh(vc.index[::-1], vc.values[::-1], color=SERIES[code]["color"], height=0.6)
        ax.set_title(f"{title}")
        ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
        for y, v in enumerate(vc.values[::-1]):
            ax.text(v, y, f" {v:,} ({v / n:.0%})", va="center", fontsize=8, color=INK_2)
        ax.set_xlim(0, vc.max() * 1.35)
    fig.suptitle(f"{SERIES[code]['name']} ({code}) — who the {n:,} feedbacks come from", x=0.01, ha="left",
                 fontweight="bold")
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    # Feedback-type mix per powertrain (share of feedbacks tagged with each type; one feedback can carry several).
    mix = pd.DataFrame({t: f.groupby("powertrain")["ftypes"].apply(lambda s: s.map(lambda x: t in x).mean())
                        for t in FEEDBACK_TYPES})
    mix["unclassified"] = f.groupby("powertrain")["ftypes"].apply(lambda s: s.map(len).eq(0).mean())
    mix.insert(0, "feedbacks", f.groupby("powertrain").size())
    display(Markdown("**Share of feedbacks tagged with each feedback type, by powertrain**"))
    display(mix.style.format({c: "{:.0%}" for c in mix.columns if c != "feedbacks"}).format({"feedbacks": "{:,}"}))


def topic_table(code, min_rows=10):
    r = fb_rows[(fb_rows["series"] == code) & fb_rows["classified"]]
    t = r.pivot_table(index="topic", columns="ftype", values="ID", aggfunc="count", fill_value=0)
    t = t.reindex(columns=FEEDBACK_TYPES, fill_value=0)
    t["total"] = t.sum(axis=1)
    t["feedbacks"] = r.groupby("topic")["ID"].nunique()
    t["net_sentiment"] = (t["Likes"] - t[["Difficult to Use", "Defect", "Wants"]].sum(axis=1)) / t["total"]
    t["pain"] = t[["Difficult to Use", "Defect"]].sum(axis=1)
    return t[t["total"] >= min_rows].sort_values("total", ascending=False)


def plot_topics(code, top=15):
    t = topic_table(code).head(top)[FEEDBACK_TYPES].iloc[::-1]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 0.36 * top + 1))
    left = np.zeros(len(t))
    for ft in FEEDBACK_TYPES:
        ax.barh([short(i, 45) for i in t.index], t[ft], left=left, color=TYPE_COLORS[ft], label=ft,
                height=0.65, edgecolor="white", linewidth=1)
        left += t[ft].values
    for y, v in enumerate(left):
        ax.text(v, y, f" {v:,.0f}", va="center", fontsize=8, color=INK_2)
    ax.set_title(f"{SERIES[code]['name']} ({code}) — top {top} topics by classified rows, split by feedback type")
    ax.legend(ncol=4, loc="lower right")
    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    plt.show()


def topic_rankings(code, n=10):
    t = topic_table(code)
    views = {
        "Most liked (Likes rows)": t.sort_values("Likes", ascending=False)["Likes"],
        "Biggest pain points (Difficult to Use + Defect rows)": t.sort_values("pain", ascending=False)["pain"],
        "Most wanted (Wants rows)": t.sort_values("Wants", ascending=False)["Wants"],
    }
    side_by_side = pd.concat(
        [pd.DataFrame({(title, "topic"): s.head(n).index, (title, "rows"): s.head(n).values}) for title, s in views.items()],
        axis=1,
    )
    side_by_side.index = range(1, n + 1)
    display(side_by_side)
    display(Markdown("**Most polarising topics (≥ 25 rows): lowest net sentiment**"))
    display(t[t["total"] >= 25].sort_values("net_sentiment").head(n)[FEEDBACK_TYPES + ["total", "net_sentiment"]]
            .style.format({"net_sentiment": "{:+.2f}"}).background_gradient(subset="net_sentiment", cmap="RdBu", vmin=-1, vmax=1))


def wants_detail(code, n=12):
    """What kind of request customers make (level 3) and for which topic."""
    r = fb_rows[(fb_rows["series"] == code) & (fb_rows["ftype"] == "Wants")]
    out = r.groupby(["topic", "nature"]).size().sort_values(ascending=False).head(n).to_frame("rows")
    display(Markdown("**Wants: top topic × request type**"))
    display(out)


def sample_verbatims(code, topic, ftypes=("Difficult to Use", "Defect", "Wants"), k=4, seed=0):
    ids = fb_rows[(fb_rows["series"] == code) & (fb_rows["topic"] == topic) & fb_rows["ftype"].isin(ftypes)]["ID"].unique()
    picks = feedbacks.set_index("ID").loc[ids].sample(min(k, len(ids)), random_state=seed)
    lines = [f"- `{i}` ({r.Source}, {r.Country}, {r.powertrain}): {short(r.text, 260)}" for i, r in picks.iterrows()]
    display(Markdown(f"**{topic}** — {len(ids)} critical feedbacks, sample:\n\n" + "\n".join(lines)))


def source_c_severity(code):
    """Source C (US quality survey) encodes severity in the text: 'I had a <severity> problem with …'."""
    f = feedbacks[(feedbacks["series"] == code) & (feedbacks["Source"] == "C")]
    sev = f["text"].str.extract(r"I had an? (very minor|minor|serious|very serious) problem", expand=False)
    item = f["text"].str.extract(r"problem with (.+?)(?: - |:|$)", expand=False)
    d = pd.DataFrame({"severity": sev, "item": item}).dropna()
    if d.empty:
        return
    order = ["very minor", "minor", "serious", "very serious"]
    display(Markdown(f"**Source C problem reports: {len(d)} of {len(f)} Source C feedbacks state a severity**"))
    display(d["severity"].value_counts().reindex(order, fill_value=0).to_frame("feedbacks").T)
    serious = d[d["severity"].isin(["serious", "very serious"])]["item"].value_counts().head(10)
    display(Markdown("Items with the most *serious / very serious* problems:"))
    display(serious.to_frame("feedbacks").T)


def study_cneu_profile(code):
    cols = [c for c in study_cneu.columns if c.endswith(code) or (code == "G60" and c.endswith("G68"))]
    attrs = study_cneu.drop(index="Overall product satisfaction")
    peer_mean = attrs.mean(axis=1)
    for col in cols:
        s = attrs[col]
        gap = (s - attrs.drop(columns=col).mean(axis=1)).rename("vs other columns")
        overall = study_cneu.loc["Overall product satisfaction", col]
        d = pd.DataFrame({"score": s, "rank (of 36)": s.rank(ascending=False).astype(int), "vs other columns": gap})
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 7.5))
        ds = d.sort_values("score")
        hatch = "///" if col.endswith("G68") else None
        ax.barh(ds.index, ds["score"], color=SERIES[code]["color"], height=0.65, hatch=hatch, edgecolor="white")
        ax.scatter(peer_mean.loc[ds.index], ds.index, marker="|", s=120, color=INK, zorder=3,
                   label="mean of all 5 study columns")
        ax.set_xlim(6, 10.2)
        ax.axvline(overall, color=INK_2, linestyle="--", linewidth=1, label=f"overall satisfaction {overall:.2f}")
        ax.set_title(f"Customer study {col} — mean score per attribute")
        ax.legend(loc="lower right")
        ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
        ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=8)
        plt.show()
        display(Markdown(f"**{col}: weakest and strongest attributes** (gap = score minus the mean of the other four columns)"))
        both = pd.concat([d.nsmallest(6, "score").assign(group="weakest"), d.nlargest(4, "score").assign(group="strongest")])
        display(both.style.format({"score": "{:.2f}", "vs other columns": "{:+.2f}"})
                .background_gradient(subset="vs other columns", cmap="RdBu", vmin=-1.5, vmax=1.5))


def study_us_profile(code, n=10):
    u = study_us[study_us["series"] == code].set_index("attribute")
    other = study_us[study_us["series"] != code].set_index("attribute")
    u = u.assign(top2_vs_other=u["top2"] - other["top2"])
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.8))
    pick = pd.concat([u.nlargest(n, "bottom3"), u.nsmallest(n // 2, "bottom3")]).drop_duplicates().sort_values("bottom3")
    ax.barh([short(i, 50) for i in pick.index], pick["bottom3"], color="#e34948", height=0.6, label="bottom-3 box")
    ax.barh([short(i, 50) for i in pick.index], -pick["top2"], color=SERIES[code]["color"], height=0.6, label="top-2 box")
    ax.axvline(0, color=INK_2, linewidth=0.8)
    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(lambda v, _: f"{abs(v) * 100:.0f}%")
    ax.set_title(f"US study {code} — most-disliked attributes (top) vs least-disliked (bottom)")
    ax.legend(ncol=2, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.1))
    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=8)
    plt.show()
    other_code = "G70" if code == "G60" else "G60"
    display(Markdown(f"**US {code}: lowest weighted mean (1–7)**, with the top-2 gap vs the {other_code}"))
    display(u.nsmallest(n, "mean_1_7")[["mean_1_7", "top2", "bottom3", "top2_vs_other"]]
            .style.format({"mean_1_7": "{:.2f}", "top2": "{:.0%}", "bottom3": "{:.1%}", "top2_vs_other": "{:+.0%}"}))


def equipment_profile(code):
    models, items, model_names = options[code]
    cols = [c for c in models.columns
            if re.search(r"^Model$|Fuel|^Drive|output|range|price", c, re.I) and not re.search(r"Combustion|E-motor|48 V", c)]
    display(Markdown(f"**Models in the German catalog ({len(models)})**"))
    display(models[cols].set_index("Model"))

    covered = [m for m in model_names if (items[m] != "n/a").any()]
    counts = pd.DataFrame({m: items[m].value_counts() for m in covered}).reindex(["S", "O", "–"]).fillna(0).astype(int)
    counts.index = ["standard (S)", "optional (O)", "not offered (–)"]
    display(Markdown(f"**Equipment rows per model** (standard + optional equipment sections, {len(items)} items; "
                     f"{len(model_names) - len(covered)} models have no equipment data)"))
    display(counts)

    by_cat = (items.melt(id_vars=["section", "category"], value_vars=covered, var_name="model", value_name="avail")
              .query("avail == 'S'").groupby(["category", "model"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0)[covered])
    display(Markdown("**Standard (S) items per category and model**"))
    display(by_cat.style.background_gradient(cmap="Blues", axis=None))

    # Items that are optional or missing on at least one model while standard on another: the trim ladder.
    s_any = (items[covered] == "S").any(axis=1)
    not_s_any = (items[covered] != "S").any(axis=1)
    ladder = items[s_any & not_s_any][["category", "code", "item", *covered]]
    display(Markdown(f"**Trim ladder: {len(ladder)} items that are standard on some models but not on others**"))
    display(ladder.assign(item=ladder["item"].map(lambda s: short(s, 70))).set_index(["category", "code"]))

content.content:
# Sales volumes: `sales_volumes.xlsx`

Units per market. There is one sheet per vehicle, each with the same columns: `market`, `market_code`, `volume_2024`, `volume_2025`, `volume_2030`.

> The BMW data slide describes this dataset as "units by powertrain and region", but **the file has no powertrain split**, only markets. Powertrain mix has to come from elsewhere (e.g. the `Engine Type` share in the feedback files, which is not a sales share).
> `volume_2030` is presumably a **forecast/plan** (inferred; not stated).

## F70: BMW 1 Series (sheet `F70`)

| Market | Code | 2024 | 2025 | 2030 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Europe | EU | 80,000 | 85,000 | 87,000 |
| China | CN | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| USA | US | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Rest of World | RoW | 25,000 | 28,000 | 31,000 |
| **Total** | | **105,000** | **113,000** | **118,000** |

## G60 / G68: BMW 5 Series (sheet `G60_G68`, sedan and long wheelbase combined)

| Market | Code | 2024 | 2025 | 2030 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Europe | EU | 110,000 | 115,000 | 127,000 |
| China | CN | 68,000 | 75,000 | 78,000 |
| USA | US | 75,600 | 78,000 | 80,000 |
| Rest of World | RoW | 25,000 | 28,000 | 31,000 |
| **Total** | | **278,600** | **296,000** | **316,000** |

## G70: BMW 7 Series (sheet `G70`)

| Market | Code | 2024 | 2025 | 2030 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Europe | EU | 11,000 | 13,000 | 17,000 |
| China | CN | 8,000 | 10,000 | 12,000 |
| USA | US | 10,000 | 12,000 | 14,000 |
| Rest of World | RoW | 5,000 | 7,000 | 9,000 |
| **Total** | | **34,000** | **42,000** | **52,000** |

## What this means for choosing a demo scope

- **1 Series = Europe (+ RoW) only.** A 1 Series demo only makes sense for EU. Its feedback is mostly GB, and its customer study covers EU only.
- **5 Series is the volume car**: ~2.6× the 1 Series in 2025 and selling in all three focus markets. In China it is the G68 long wheelbase; China has customer-study data (G68) but no feedback.
- **7 Series is small in volume (~42k)** but the most balanced across EU/CN/US. It has the most US feedback and has study data in all three regions.
- Projected growth 2025 → 2030: F70 +4 %, G60/G68 +7 %, G70 +24 %.
- The 5 Series sheet mixes G60 and G68, so per-derivative volumes are not available.

## Data coverage by vehicle and market

| | EU | CN | US |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **F70** | sales ✓ · study ✓ · feedback (GB, SE, FR, DK, FI) | no sales | no sales |
| **G60** | sales ✓ · study ✓ · feedback thin | sales (as G68) | sales ✓ · study ✓ · feedback ✓✓ |
| **G68** | – | sales (combined with G60) · study ✓ · no feedback | – |
| **G70** | sales ✓ · study ✓ · feedback thin | sales ✓ · study ✓ · no feedback | sales ✓ · study ✓ · feedback ✓✓ |
# Customer verbatims: `*_feedback_hackathon.xlsx`

Free-text customer feedback on the current vehicle, already tagged by BMW with a feedback classification (VFC). One file per vehicle:

| File | Vehicle | Rows | Unique feedbacks (IDs) | Max rows per ID |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `data/F70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` | BMW 1 Series (F70) | 4,076 | 2,128 | 11 |
| `data/G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` | BMW 5 Series (G60) | 5,005 | 4,000 | 18 |
| `data/G70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` | BMW 7 Series (G70) | 4,690 | 4,000 | 17 |

Each file has a single sheet, `Feedback_Explorer`.

> **One row = one classification, not one feedback.** A verbatim that mentions several topics appears once per topic, with the same `ID` and the same text. Always count unique `ID`s when you count feedbacks. All rows of one ID carry identical text (verified).

Labels: **observed** means checked in the data. **Inferred** means our reading; BMW has not confirmed it.

## Columns

| Column | Meaning | Values (observed) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ID` | Feedback ID, `<e-code>-<nnnn>` | F70-0001…F70-2128, G60-0001…G60-4000, G70-0001…G70-4000 |
| `Source` | Anonymized feedback channel | `Source A`–`Source D` (see below) |
| `Brand` | Brand | always `[BMW]` |
| `Sales Description` | Model series | `[BMW 1 Series]`, `[BMW 5 Series]`, `[BMW 7 Series]` (one per file) |
| `Country` | ISO country code of the customer | see coverage below |
| `Derivate (e-code)` | Vehicle derivative | `F70`, `G60`, `G70` (one per file; **no G68 rows** in the G60 file) |
| `Engine Type` | Powertrain | `ICE`, `PHEV`, `BEVE` (inferred: BEVE = battery-electric, i.e. i5 / i7) |
| `Feedback Type` | Coarse sentiment/type | `Likes`, `Difficult to Use`, `Defect`, `Wants`, empty |
| `Customer Feedback` | The verbatim (English) | median ~140–150 characters, max 1,554 (F70) / 3,498 (G60) / 4,260 (G70) |
| `Vfc level2 3 Name` | `"<level2> : <level3>"` concatenated | redundant with the next two columns (matches in >99.9 % of rows) |
| `Vfc level2 Name` | **Topic / component** (what the feedback is about) | 120 (F70), 221 (G60), 211 (G70) distinct values; 226 across all files; plus `no_class_found` or empty |
| `Vfc level3 Name` | **Nature of the statement** (like / defect / request …) | 57 (F70), 82 (G60), 77 (G70) distinct values |

## Feedback sources

BMW does not explain the sources. The descriptions below are **inferred** from how the texts read.

| Source | Style of text | Countries | Vehicles | Inferred channel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | First person, mostly lowercase, review-like: *"really solid build, lots of attention to detail. i only knock off one mark because there's no paper user manual."* | Many (GB, JP, KR, US, SE, FR, …) | F70, G60, G70; **the only source for F70** | Owner reviews / online or app feedback |
| **B** | Third-person paraphrase: *"Customer stated the vehicle provides a quiet, peaceful ride."* | US only | G60, G70 | Dealer, call-centre or interview notes |
| **C** | Survey answers: *"I had a very serious problem with \<item> - \<symptom>: "…""*, plus open questions such as *"What is the primary reason for your nps rating?"* | US only | G60, G70 | Quality / NPS survey with severity levels |
| **D** | *"\<answer>. That is the one thing I love most about / could be most improved about \<area> of my vehicle."* | US only | G60, G70 | Structured survey open-ends |

### Unique feedbacks per source

| Source | F70 | G60 | G70 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A | 2,128 | 854 | 695 |
| B | – | 2,626 | 2,853 |
| C | – | 384 | 314 |
| D | – | 136 | 138 |

## Coverage

### Countries (unique feedbacks)

| Vehicle | Countries |
| --- | --- |
| F70 | GB 1,293 · JP 672 · SE 71 · FR 53 · AU 16 · FI 8 · DK 8 · KR 4 · ZA 3 |

Yes. The 5 Series (G60) in the US has all three kinds of data, so it works as your one series and one location. Here's what's there:

| Requirement | 5 Series · US | How it compares |
|---|---|---|
| **Sales** | 75,600 (2024) → 78,000 (2025) → 80,000 (2030, presumably a forecast) | The 5 Series is the biggest-selling car in the challenge data. Its US volume is about 6× the 7 Series in the US, and the 1 Series isn't sold there at all. |
| **Customer feedback** | **3,610 unique feedbacks**, which is about 90% of all G60 feedback | This is the strongest of any market. Europe has only a few dozen, and China and Germany have none. |
| **Customer study** | A US 2025 sheet with about **100 rated attributes** on a 7-point scale ("I Hate It" → "I Love It") | It includes a 7 Series column next to it, so you can compare the two. |

The US feedback for the 5 Series is also well spread:
- **Engine types:** 2,017 petrol/diesel, 1,271 electric (i5) and 322 plug-in hybrid. That means you can also cover the electric car.
- **Feedback types:** 1,694 Likes, 1,217 Difficult to Use, 532 Wants and 377 Defects, across 221 topics.
- **Channels:** four different ones (Sources A to D). The structured survey channels (C and D) are US-only.

**Caveats:**
- **Sales:** The sales file combines the regular 5 Series (G60) with the long-wheelbase version (G68). That doesn't matter for the US, because the long-wheelbase version is sold in China, but the 78k figure is still a combined number. The file also doesn't split sales by engine type.
- **Feedback:** Most of it (2,626 of 3,610) comes from one channel, Source B. It looks like dealer or call-centre notes, so it's paraphrased rather than in the customer's own words.
- **Survey:** The US survey uses a different scale from the China/EU survey and gives no sample sizes, so don't compare US scores directly with Europe or China.

The 5 Series in Europe would be the only other choice with real sales volume. It has the most sales of any series and market (115k), but its feedback is very thin, so the US is the better pick.

The 5 Series in the US is the best choice. Only two other combinations have all three kinds of data: the 7 Series in the US and the 1 Series in Europe.

| Series · Market | Sales 2025 | Unique feedbacks | Customer study | All three? |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| **5 Series (G60) · US** | **78,000** | **3,610** | ✓ US sheet | **✓ best overall** |
| 7 Series (G70) · US | 12,000 | 3,792 | ✓ US sheet | ✓ but small volume |
| 1 Series (F70) · Europe | 85,000 | ~1,430 (1,293 of them from GB) | ✓ EU sheet | ✓ but mostly UK feedback |
| 5 Series (G60) · Europe | 115,000 | ~110 | ✓ EU sheet | ✗ too little feedback |
| 7 Series (G70) · Europe | 13,000 | ~19 | ✓ EU sheet | ✗ |
| 5 Series (G68) · China | 75,000 (combined with G60) | 0 | ✓ CN sheet | ✗ no feedback |
| 7 Series (G70) · China | 10,000 | 0 | ✓ CN sheet | ✗ no feedback |
| 1 Series · US or China | 0 | 0 | ✗ | ✗ not sold there |
| Any series · Rest of World | 7k–28k | 189–695 (mostly Japan and Korea) | ✗ | ✗ no study |

**The two alternatives, compared with the 5 Series in the US:**
- **7 Series · US:** It has slightly more feedback (3,792) and the same US survey. It sells only about 12k cars, though, which is about 6× fewer than the 5 Series in the US. It's still a fair choice if your pitch is about luxury or flagship features rather than volume. It's also forecast to grow fastest (+24% to 2030).
- **1 Series · Europe:** It has real volume (85k), but its feedback is all from owner reviews (Source A), and the only engine type in it is petrol/diesel. About 90% of that feedback is from the UK, and there's none from Germany. The China/EU survey also gives no sample sizes.

**Ruled out:**
- **China:** there's no feedback for any series.

This notebook profiles every vehicle series in the BMW challenge data, one section per series, then compares them side by side.

Data caveats from `docs/datasets/` that shape every number below:

- Feedback files hold **one row per classification**. Feedback counts use unique `ID`s; topic counts use rows (one feedback can raise several topics).

def iter_md_tables(path):
    """Yield (h2, h3, header, cells) for every Markdown table row in a file."""
    h2 = h3 = header = None
    for line in Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("## "):
            h2, h3, header = line[3:].strip(), None, None
        elif line.startswith("### "):
            h3, header = line[4:].strip(), None
        elif line.startswith("|"):
            cells = [c.strip().replace("\\|", "|") for c in re.split(r"(?<!\\)\|", line.strip().strip("|"))]
            if header is None:
                header = cells
            elif not set("".join(cells)) <= set("-: "):
                yield h2, h3, header, cells
        else:

Everything BMW gave us about the challenge, consolidated in one place (EHL Munich 2026 final, TUM.ai, 10–11 Oct 2026).

**Sources** (originals in [`sources/`](sources/)):

| # | Source | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S1 | [`BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf`](sources/BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf) | Official 2-page briefing (BMW Group) |
| S2 | Detailed mission text (shared by BMW, pasted by the team) | Sections 1–5: mission, scope, "make it yours", deliverables |
| S3 | [`slide-data-and-sources.png`](sources/slide-data-and-sources.png) | Table "Data and sources — provided data (per vehicle)" |
| S4 | [`slide-billions-of-findings-to-one-vehicle.webp`](sources/slide-billions-of-findings-to-one-vehicle.webp) | Slide "From billions of findings to one BMW vehicle" |
| S5 | [`slide-the-process.webp`](sources/slide-the-process.webp) | Slide "The process" (BMW's requirements workflow) |

Where S1 and S2 differ in wording or emphasis, both are kept and marked.

---

## 1. The challenge in one paragraph

*What should the next generation of a BMW vehicle offer its customers?* Build an AI-powered application that helps product managers (PMs) **derive, justify and prioritize customer requirements for a successor vehicle**. Ground the proposals in customer feedback, BMW product and sales data, and relevant web research, while keeping **the PM firmly in control of every decision**. (S1)

## 2. Why this matters (S1)

- Defining a new vehicle generation means understanding what customers value today **and** anticipating what they will value when the successor reaches the market.
- PMs turn large volumes of customer feedback, market signals, competitor information and product data into well-founded product requirements.
- Today this work is largely **manual, time-consuming and hard to trace consistently**.
- AI could help PMs identify relevant insights, formulate requirements and justify prioritization decisions more efficiently, while keeping **evidence, assumptions and uncertainties transparent and under human control**.

## 3. Mission

### 3.1 Short version (S1)

Develop an application that helps PMs **define, explain and prioritize customer-facing requirements for the successor of an existing BMW vehicle line**.

- **Vehicles:** BMW 1 Series, 5 Series, 7 Series, or a combination.
- **Markets:** Europe, China, the United States, or any subset that best demonstrates the approach.
- **Time horizon:** think **3–5 years ahead**. Which customer needs and expectations should shape the next generation?
- Make clear **where conclusions rest on available evidence and where they rely on forward-looking assumptions**.
- For each vehicle BMW provides **customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study**. Teams may enrich these with external sources (competitor information, reviews, market or technology trends).
- BMW cares about **how the solution turns diverse information into actionable PM insights and makes its reasoning transparent**, not about a specific workflow or technical architecture.

### 3.2 Detailed version (S2, section 1 "Your mission")

Build an AI-powered application that ingests heterogeneous data, derives customer requirements for a vehicle, prioritizes them, and puts a PM in the loop at the decisions that matter. The app should be able to:

1. **Ingest** the provided data and enrich it with structured knowledge from the web.
2. **Extract signals** such as recurring complaints, unmet needs, competitor advantages and market trends, **each linked to its sources**.
3. **Derive requirements** from those findings: clear, actionable, customer-facing and realistic.
4. **Prioritize** them with a logic we define and can explain.
5. **Involve the PM** to approve, reject, edit or challenge requirements, along with the rationale and evidence behind them.
6. **Record everything in an audit trail**: a complete, chronological record of all actions, changes and access events within the system.

## 4. Scope (S2, section 2)

| In scope: customer requirements on the product | Out of scope |
| --- | --- |
| Features and equipment | Regulatory and homologation requirements (e.g. safety, emissions, type approval) |
| Comfort and space | Technical and engineering requirements (e.g. component specs, architecture, supplier topics) |
| Usability | Pricing, business case and cost calculation. **Cost or effort may be used as a rough prioritization factor.** |
| Infotainment and digital services | |

def iter_md_tables(path):
    """Yield (h2, h3, header, cells) for every Markdown table row in a file."""
    h2 = h3 = header = None
    for line in Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("## "):
            h2, h3, header = line[3:].strip(), None, None
        elif line.startswith("### "):
            h3, header = line[4:].strip(), None
        elif line.startswith("|"):
            cells = [c.strip().replace("\\|", "|") for c in re.split(r"(?<!\\)\|", line.strip().strip("|"))]
            if header is None:
                header = cells
            elif not set("".join(cells)) <= set("-: "):
                yield h2, h3, header, cells
        else:
            header = None

## 1. The challenge in one paragraph

*What should the next generation of a BMW vehicle offer its customers?* Build an AI-powered application that helps product managers (PMs) **derive, justify and prioritize customer requirements for a successor vehicle**. Ground the proposals in customer feedback, BMW product and sales data, and relevant web research, while keeping **the PM firmly in control of every decision**. (S1)

## 2. Why this matters (S1)

- Defining a new vehicle generation means understanding what customers value today **and** anticipating what they will value when the successor reaches the market.
- PMs turn large volumes of customer feedback, market signals, competitor information and product data into well-founded product requirements.
- Today this work is largely **manual, time-consuming and hard to trace consistently**.
- AI could help PMs identify relevant insights, formulate requirements and justify prioritization decisions more efficiently, while keeping **evidence, assumptions and uncertainties transparent and under human control**.

## 3. Mission

### 3.1 Short version (S1)

Develop an application that helps PMs **define, explain and prioritize customer-facing requirements for the successor of an existing BMW vehicle line**.

- **Vehicles:** BMW 1 Series, 5 Series, 7 Series, or a combination.
- **Markets:** Europe, China, the United States, or any subset that best demonstrates the approach.
- **Time horizon:** think **3–5 years ahead**. Which customer needs and expectations should shape the next generation?
- Make clear **where conclusions rest on available evidence and where they rely on forward-looking assumptions**.
- For each vehicle BMW provides **customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study**. Teams may enrich these with external sources (competitor information, reviews, market or technology trends).
- BMW cares about **how the solution turns diverse information into actionable PM insights and makes its reasoning transparent**, not about a specific workflow or technical architecture.

### 3.2 Detailed version (S2, section 1 "Your mission")

Build an AI-powered application that ingests heterogeneous data, derives customer requirements for a vehicle, prioritizes them, and puts a PM in the loop at the decisions that matter. The app should be able to:

1. **Ingest** the provided data and enrich it with structured knowledge from the web.
2. **Extract signals** such as recurring complaints, unmet needs, competitor advantages and market trends, **each linked to its sources**.
3. **Derive requirements** from those findings: clear, actionable, customer-facing and realistic.
4. **Prioritize** them with a logic we define and can explain.
5. **Involve the PM** to approve, reject, edit or challenge requirements, along with the rationale and evidence behind them.
6. **Record everything in an audit trail**: a complete, chronological record of all actions, changes and access events within the system.

## 4. Scope (S2, section 2)

| In scope: customer requirements on the product | Out of scope |
| --- | --- |
| Features and equipment | Regulatory and homologation requirements (e.g. safety, emissions, type approval) |
| Comfort and space | Technical and engineering requirements (e.g. component specs, architecture, supplier topics) |
| Usability | Pricing, business case and cost calculation. **Cost or effort may be used as a rough prioritization factor.** |
| Infotainment and digital services | |
| Design and quality perception | |
| Driving experience | |
| Range and charging **as experienced by the customer** | |
| Variant and package offering, etc. | |

S1 says the same in short form: focus on **customer value** rather than engineering specifications, regulatory requirements or detailed business-case calculations.

## 5. Make it yours

- Demonstrate the application for **at least one derivative in one market**. Don't design it as a one-off: it should be **adaptable to other BMW vehicles and markets**. The remaining datasets and scenarios are available for optional testing. (S2)
- The challenge is broad on purpose. Focus where the team can contribute most, for example (S1 + S2):
  - going deep on **web research** and turning external information into usable evidence,
  - integrating and interpreting the **provided BMW data**,
  - uncovering customer insights, formulating compelling requirements, improving prioritization,
  - designing an effective **human-in-the-loop** experience.
- Not every capability needs the same maturity, but **show how the chosen focus connects to the full path from evidence to PM decision**. (S2)
- Consider how the concept scales across vehicle lines, markets and future product decisions. (S1)
- **What BMW values (S1):** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, and a clear understanding of **uncertainty and conflicting evidence**.

EQUIPMENT_SECTIONS = {"Standard equipment (Serienausstattung)", "Optional equipment (Sonderausstattungen)"}
AVAIL_RANK = {"S": 2, "O": 1}


def iter_md_tables(path):
    """Yield (h2, h3, header, cells) for every Markdown table row in a file."""
    h2 = h3 = header = None
    for line in Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("## "):
            h2, h3, header = line[3:].strip(), None, None
        elif line.startswith("### "):
            h3, header = line[4:].strip(), None
        elif line.startswith("|"):
            cells = [c.strip().replace("\\|", "|") for c in re.split(r"(?<!\\)\|", line.strip().strip("|"))]
            if header is None:
                header = cells
            elif not set("".join(cells)) <= set("-: "):
                yield h2, h3, header, cells
        else:
            header = None


def parse_option_list(path):
    rows = list(iter_md_tables(path))
    models = pd.DataFrame(
        [dict(zip(h, c)) for h2, _, h, c in rows if h2 == "Models & powertrains" and h[0] == "Model"]
    )
    model_names = models["Model"].tolist()

    items = []
    for h2, h3, header, cells in rows:
        if h2 not in EQUIPMENT_SECTIONS:
            continue
        row = dict(zip(header, cells))
        name = row.get("Name (DE)") or row.get("Item (DE)") or ""
        code = row.get("Code") or row.get("Code¹") or row.get("Code (cross-ref)") or ""
        avail = {m: row[m] for m in model_names if m in row}
        if not avail:
            continue
        if name.startswith("↳") and items:  # price variant of the item above
            parent = items[-1]
            for m, v in avail.items():
                if AVAIL_RANK.get(v, 0) > AVAIL_RANK.get(parent[m], 0):
                    parent[m] = v
            continue
        items.append({"section": "standard" if h2.startswith("Standard") else "optional",
                      "category": re.sub(r"\s*\(.*?\)\s*$", "", h3 or ""), "code": code,
                      "item": name, **{m: avail.get(m, "n/a") for m in model_names}})
    return models, pd.DataFrame(items), model_names


options = {code: parse_option_list(OPTION_DOCS / meta["option_doc"]) for code, meta in SERIES.items()}

def topic_table(code, min_rows=10):
    r = fb_rows[(fb_rows["series"] == code) & fb_rows["classified"]]
    t = r.pivot_table(index="topic", columns="ftype", values="ID", aggfunc="count", fill_value=0)
    t = t.reindex(columns=FEEDBACK_TYPES, fill_value=0)
    t["total"] = t.sum(axis=1)
    t["feedbacks"] = r.groupby("topic")["ID"].nunique()
    t["net_sentiment"] = (t["Likes"] - t[["Difficult to Use", "Defect", "Wants"]].sum(axis=1)) / t["total"]
    t["pain"] = t[["Difficult to Use", "Defect"]].sum(axis=1)
    return t[t["total"] >= min_rows].sort_values("total", ascending=False)

EQUIPMENT_SECTIONS = {"Standard equipment (Serienausstattung)", "Optional equipment (Sonderausstattungen)"}
AVAIL_RANK = {"S": 2, "O": 1}


def iter_md_tables(path):
    """Yield (h2, h3, header, cells) for every Markdown table row in a file."""
    h2 = h3 = header = None
    for line in Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("## "):
            h2, h3, header = line[3:].strip(), None, None
        elif line.startswith("### "):
            h3, header = line[4:].strip(), None
        elif line.startswith("|"):
            cells = [c.strip().replace("\\|", "|") for c in re.split(r"(?<!\\)\|", line.strip().strip("|"))]
            if header is None:
                header = cells
            elif not set("".join(cells)) <= set("-: "):
                yield h2, h3, header, cells
        else:
            header = None


def parse_option_list(path):
    rows = list(iter_md_tables(path))
    models = pd.DataFrame(
        [dict(zip(h, c)) for h2, _, h, c in rows if h2 == "Models & powertrains" and h[0] == "Model"]
    )
    model_names = models["Model"].tolist()

    items = []
    for h2, h3, header, cells in rows:
        if h2 not in EQUIPMENT_SECTIONS:
            continue
        row = dict(zip(header, cells))
        name = row.get("Name (DE)") or row.get("Item (DE)") or ""
        code = row.get("Code") or row.get("Code¹") or row.get("Code (cross-ref)") or ""
        avail = {m: row[m] for m in model_names if m in row}
        if not avail:
            continue
        if name.startswith("↳") and items:  # price variant of the item above
            parent = items[-1]
            for m, v in avail.items():
                if AVAIL_RANK.get(v, 0) > AVAIL_RANK.get(parent[m], 0):
                    parent[m] = v
            continue
        items.append({"section": "standard" if h2.startswith("Standard") else "optional",
                      "category": re.sub(r"\s*\(.*?\)\s*$", "", h3 or ""), "code": code,
                      "item": name, **{m: avail.get(m, "n/a") for m in model_names}})
    return models, pd.DataFrame(items), model_names

def topic_table(code, min_rows=10):
    r = fb_rows[(fb_rows["series"] == code) & fb_rows["classified"]]
    t = r.pivot_table(index="topic", columns="ftype", values="ID", aggfunc="count", fill_value=0)
    t = t.reindex(columns=FEEDBACK_TYPES, fill_value=0)
    t["total"] = t.sum(axis=1)
    t["feedbacks"] = r.groupby("topic")["ID"].nunique()
    t["net_sentiment"] = (t["Likes"] - t[["Difficult to Use", "Defect", "Wants"]].sum(axis=1)) / t["total"]
    t["pain"] = t[["Difficult to Use", "Defect"]].sum(axis=1)
    return t[t["total"] >= min_rows].sort_values("total", ascending=False)

"""Generate notebooks/g60_us_analysis.ipynb (BMW 5 Series G60, US market deep dive)."""
import sys
import nbformat as nbf

OUT = sys.argv[1]
cells = []


def md(s):
    cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(s.strip("\n")))


def code(s):
    cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(s.strip("\n")))


md(r"""
# BMW 5 Series (G60) · United States — focus analysis

The hackathon asks for **one derivative in one market**. This notebook takes the 5 Series sedan (G60) in the US and goes
through all the BMW data for it. Each section ends with a short set of findings. The last sections combine everything
into an evidence table that can feed the requirements app.

| Dataset | File in `data/` | US 5 Series slice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sales volumes | `sales_volumes.xlsx` (sheet `G60_G68`) | US units 2024, 2025, 2030 (2030 presumably a plan) |
| Customer verbatims | `G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` | `Country == "US"`: 3,610 unique feedbacks from Sources A–D |
| Customer study | `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx` (sheet `US_2025`) | 103 attributes rated on a 7-point scale; the G70 column is used as a benchmark |

**Caveats that shape every number below** (details in `docs/datasets/`):

- Sales have **no powertrain split**, and the G60 sheet also counts the G68 (long wheelbase), which is sold in China, not the US.
- Feedback files hold **one row per classification**. Feedback counts use unique `ID`s, and topic counts use rows.
- The feedback is **not a random sample of buyers**. Source B (dealer/call-centre paraphrases) is 73 % of it, and the
  powertrain mix of feedback is not the sales mix.
- The US study gives **shares per scale point but no sample size**, so we cannot test significance.
- Equipment lists are German catalogs and are not used here.

Run from the repository root or from `notebooks/`. The raw files must be in `data/` (they are not in git).
""")

code(r"""
from pathlib import Path
import re
import textwrap

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import PercentFormatter
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

ROOT = Path.cwd() if (Path.cwd() / "data").exists() else Path.cwd().parent
DATA = ROOT / "data"

pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 120)
pd.set_option("display.width", 160)

# Same palette as series_analysis.ipynb so charts read as one system.
G60_COLOR, G70_COLOR = "#eb6834", "#1baf7a"
FEEDBACK_TYPES = ["Likes", "Difficult to Use", "Defect", "Wants"]
TYPE_COLORS = {"Likes": "#1baf7a", "Difficult to Use": "#eda100", "Defect": "#e34948", "Wants": "#6250d6"}
PT_COLORS = {"ICE": "#52514e", "BEV": "#2a78d6", "PHEV": "#9b59b6"}
INK, INK_2, GRID = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e4e3df"
MARKET_ORDER = ["EU", "CN", "US", "RoW"]

plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.dpi": 110, "figure.facecolor": "white", "axes.facecolor": "white",
    "axes.edgecolor": GRID, "axes.labelcolor": INK_2, "axes.titlesize": 12, "axes.titleweight": "bold",
    "axes.titlelocation": "left", "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": GRID, "grid.linewidth": 0.8, "axes.axisbelow": True,
    "xtick.color": INK_2, "ytick.color": INK_2, "text.color": INK, "font.size": 10, "legend.frameon": False,
})


def short(s, n=55):
    return textwrap.shorten(str(s), n, placeholder="…")


def bar_labels(ax, fmt="{:,.0f}", pad=3):
    for c in ax.containers:
        ax.bar_label(c, labels=[fmt.format(v) if v else "" for v in c.datavalues], padding=pad,
                     color=INK_2, fontsize=8)
""")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. Sales
md(r"""
---
## 1. Sales: how big is the US 5 Series?

### 1.1 US volume over time and in context
""")

code(r"""
sales = pd.concat(
    [pd.read_excel(DATA / "sales_volumes.xlsx", sheet_name=sheet).assign(series=code)
     for code, sheet in [("F70", "F70"), ("G60", "G60_G68"), ("G70", "G70")]],
    ignore_index=True,
)
YEARS = ["volume_2024", "volume_2025", "volume_2030"]
us = sales[(sales.series == "G60") & (sales.market_code == "US")].iloc[0]
g60 = sales[sales.series == "G60"].set_index("market_code").loc[MARKET_ORDER]

summary = pd.DataFrame({
    "US 5 Series units": us[YEARS].values,
    "5 Series global units": g60[YEARS].sum().values,
    "US share of 5 Series": (us[YEARS] / g60[YEARS].sum()).values,
    "US share of all 3 series sold in US": (us[YEARS].values
                                            / sales[sales.market_code == "US"][YEARS].sum().values),
}, index=["2024", "2025", "2030 (plan)"])
display(summary.style.format({"US 5 Series units": "{:,.0f}", "5 Series global units": "{:,.0f}",
                              "US share of 5 Series": "{:.1%}", "US share of all 3 series sold in US": "{:.1%}"}))

growth = pd.DataFrame({
    "2024→2025": g60["volume_2025"] / g60["volume_2024"] - 1,
    "2025→2030 total": g60["volume_2030"] / g60["volume_2025"] - 1,
    "2025→2030 CAGR": (g60["volume_2030"] / g60["volume_2025"]) ** (1 / 5) - 1,
})
display(Markdown("**5 Series growth by market** (the US row is the one we care about)"))
growth.style.format("{:+.1%}").apply(lambda r: ["font-weight: bold" if r.name == "US" else "" for _ in r], axis=1)
""")

code(r"""
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 3.6))

ax = axes[0]
years = [2024, 2025, 2030]
ax.plot(years, us[YEARS].values, color=G60_COLOR, marker="o", linewidth=2.5, label="5 Series · US")
g70_us = sales[(sales.series == "G70") & (sales.market_code == "US")].iloc[0]
ax.plot(years, g70_us[YEARS].values, color=G70_COLOR, marker="o", linewidth=2, label="7 Series · US")
for y, v in zip(years, us[YEARS].values):
    ax.annotate(f"{v:,.0f}", (y, v), xytext=(0, 8), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=8, color=INK_2)
for y, v in zip(years, g70_us[YEARS].values):
    ax.annotate(f"{v:,.0f}", (y, v), xytext=(0, 8), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=8, color=INK_2)
ax.axvspan(2025.2, 2030.5, color=GRID, alpha=0.4, zorder=0)
ax.text(2027.8, 5000, "plan / forecast", ha="center", color=INK_2, fontsize=8)
ax.set_xticks(years)
ax.set_ylim(0, 95000)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(lambda v, _: f"{v / 1000:.0f}k")
ax.set_title("US units per year")
ax.legend(loc="center right")

ax = axes[1]
share25 = g60["volume_2025"] / g60["volume_2025"].sum()
colors = [G60_COLOR if m == "US" else GRID for m in share25.index]
ax.bar(share25.index, g60["volume_2025"], color=colors, edgecolor="white")
for i, (m, v) in enumerate(g60["volume_2025"].items()):
    ax.text(i, v, f"{v:,.0f}\n{share25[m]:.0%}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8, color=INK_2)
ax.set_ylim(0, g60["volume_2025"].max() * 1.25)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(lambda v, _: f"{v / 1000:.0f}k")
ax.set_title("5 Series 2025 units by market (CN = G68)")
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
""")

md(r"""
### 1.2 How much evidence per car sold?

A rough coverage metric: unique feedbacks per 1,000 units sold in 2025, per series and market. It shows where the
voice-of-customer data is dense enough to support requirements.
""")

code(r"""
fb_all = pd.read_excel(DATA / "G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx", dtype=str)
fb_g70 = pd.read_excel(DATA / "G70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx", dtype=str)
EU_COUNTRIES = {"GB", "SE", "DK", "FI", "NO", "FR", "LV", "ES", "DE", "IT", "NL", "BE", "AT", "PL"}


def market_of(country):
    return "US" if country == "US" else "EU" if country in EU_COUNTRIES else "CN" if country == "CN" else "RoW"


rows = []
for code, fb in [("G60", fb_all), ("G70", fb_g70)]:
    per_market = fb.drop_duplicates("ID")["Country"].map(market_of).value_counts()
    for m in MARKET_ORDER:
        units = sales[(sales.series == code) & (sales.market_code == m)]["volume_2025"].sum()
        n = per_market.get(m, 0)
        rows.append({"series": code, "market": m, "units 2025": units, "feedbacks": n,
                     "feedbacks per 1k units": n / units * 1000 if units else np.nan})
cov = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index(["series", "market"])
cov.style.format({"units 2025": "{:,.0f}", "feedbacks": "{:,.0f}", "feedbacks per 1k units": "{:.1f}"}) \
    .background_gradient(subset="feedbacks per 1k units", cmap="Oranges")
""")

md(r"""
**Sales: findings**

- The US is a **stable, mature market for the 5 Series**: about 78k units in 2025, roughly a quarter of global 5 Series
  volume, growing only about 1 % a year to 2030. A successor would mostly **defend share**, not open a new market,
  so keeping current owners (fixing pain points, protecting strengths) matters more than winning new segments.
- In the US the 5 Series sells about **6.5× the 7 Series**, so it carries the brand's US sedan volume.
- The US has by far the **densest feedback per car sold** (about 46 per 1k units). Europe has about 1 per 1k, and China none.
  The US is the only 5 Series market where requirements can rest on the customer's own words.
- **Missing:** no powertrain split (ICE vs i5 vs PHEV), no trim or price split, no monthly trend. Any powertrain
  weighting below uses the *feedback* mix, which is a proxy at best.
""")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2. Feedback load
md(r"""
---
## 2. Customer feedback: who is talking?

### 2.1 Load and tidy (US rows only)
""")

code(r"""
fb_rows = fb_all[fb_all["Country"] == "US"].rename(columns={
    "Engine Type": "powertrain", "Feedback Type": "ftype",
    "Customer Feedback": "text", "Vfc level2 Name": "topic", "Vfc level3 Name": "nature",
}).copy()
fb_rows["Source"] = fb_rows["Source"].str.replace("Source ", "", regex=False)
fb_rows["powertrain"] = fb_rows["powertrain"].replace({"BEVE": "BEV"})
fb_rows["classified"] = fb_rows["topic"].notna() & (fb_rows["topic"] != "no_class_found")

feedbacks = (
    fb_rows.groupby("ID")
    .agg(Source=("Source", "first"), powertrain=("powertrain", "first"), text=("text", "first"),
         ftypes=("ftype", lambda s: frozenset(s.dropna())),
         topics=("topic", lambda s: frozenset(t for t in s.dropna() if t != "no_class_found")),
         n_labels=("ID", "size"))
    .reset_index()
)
feedbacks["text_len"] = feedbacks["text"].str.len()
cl = fb_rows[fb_rows["classified"]]

pd.Series({
    "rows (classifications)": len(fb_rows),
    "unique feedbacks": len(feedbacks),
    "feedbacks with ≥1 topic": (feedbacks["topics"].map(len) > 0).sum(),
    "unclassified feedbacks": (feedbacks["topics"].map(len) == 0).sum(),
    "classified rows": len(cl),
    "distinct topics": cl["topic"].nunique(),
    "median text length (chars)": int(feedbacks["text_len"].median()),
}).to_frame("US 5 Series").style.format("{:,}")
""")

md("### 2.2 Source, powertrain and feedback type")

code(r"""
n = len(feedbacks)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 3))
for ax, col, title in zip(axes[:2], ["Source", "powertrain"], ["Source", "Powertrain"]):
    vc = feedbacks[col].value_counts()
    cols = [PT_COLORS.get(i, G60_COLOR) for i in vc.index]
    ax.barh(vc.index[::-1], vc.values[::-1], color=cols[::-1], height=0.6)
    for y, v in enumerate(vc.values[::-1]):
        ax.text(v, y, f" {v:,} ({v / n:.0%})", va="center", fontsize=8, color=INK_2)
    ax.set_xlim(0, vc.max() * 1.4)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)

ax = axes[2]
tshare = {t: feedbacks["ftypes"].map(lambda x: t in x).mean() for t in FEEDBACK_TYPES}
tshare["(none)"] = feedbacks["ftypes"].map(len).eq(0).mean()
ax.barh(list(tshare)[::-1], list(tshare.values())[::-1],
        color=[TYPE_COLORS.get(t, GRID) for t in list(tshare)[::-1]], height=0.6)
for y, v in enumerate(list(tshare.values())[::-1]):
    ax.text(v, y, f" {v:.0%}", va="center", fontsize=8, color=INK_2)
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(1, decimals=0))
ax.set_xlim(0, 0.65)
ax.set_title("Feedbacks tagged with type")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
fig.suptitle(f"Who the {n:,} US 5 Series feedbacks come from", x=0.01, ha="left", fontweight="bold")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

src_pt = pd.crosstab(feedbacks["Source"], feedbacks["powertrain"], margins=True)
display(Markdown("**Source × powertrain (unique feedbacks)**"))
display(src_pt)
""")

code(r"""
# Feedback-type mix per source and per powertrain: does the channel or the drivetrain change the tone?
def type_mix(by):
    out = pd.DataFrame({t: feedbacks.groupby(by)["ftypes"].apply(lambda s: s.map(lambda x: t in x).mean())
                        for t in FEEDBACK_TYPES})
    out.insert(0, "feedbacks", feedbacks.groupby(by).size())
    return out

display(Markdown("**Share of feedbacks tagged with each type, by source**"))
display(type_mix("Source").style.format({t: "{:.0%}" for t in FEEDBACK_TYPES})
        .background_gradient(subset=FEEDBACK_TYPES, cmap="Greys", axis=None))
display(Markdown("**…and by powertrain**"))
display(type_mix("powertrain").style.format({t: "{:.0%}" for t in FEEDBACK_TYPES})
        .background_gradient(subset=FEEDBACK_TYPES, cmap="Greys", axis=None))
""")

code(r"""
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3))
for src, color in zip("ABCD", ["#2a78d6", G60_COLOR, "#6250d6", "#1baf7a"]):
    lens = feedbacks.loc[feedbacks.Source == src, "text_len"].clip(upper=800)
    ax.hist(lens, bins=40, alpha=0.55, color=color, label=f"Source {src} (median {lens.median():.0f})")
ax.set_title("Text length per source (characters, clipped at 800)")
ax.set_xlabel("characters")
ax.legend()
plt.show()
""")

md(r"""
**Who is talking: findings**

- **Source B (dealer/call-centre paraphrase) is 73 %** of the data. Its text is short and third-person ("Customer
  stated…"), so it tells us *what* is wrong but rarely *why* or how badly. Severity has to come from Source C.
- About **35 % of feedback is from i5 (BEV) owners**. That makes EV-specific topics (range, charging) analysable, but
  the mix is not the sales mix, which we don't have.
- Likes are the most common tag. Difficult-to-Use is the main negative, well ahead of Defect, so the US story is
  mostly about **usability, not broken parts**.
""")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3. Topics
md(r"""
---
## 3. What customers talk about

**Net sentiment per topic** = (Likes − Difficult to Use − Defect − Wants) / all classified rows of the topic.
Wants counts as negative because it marks something the car doesn't do today. **Pain** = Difficult to Use + Defect rows.
""")

code(r"""
def topic_table(rows, min_rows=10):
    t = rows.pivot_table(index="topic", columns="ftype", values="ID", aggfunc="count", fill_value=0)
    t = t.reindex(columns=FEEDBACK_TYPES, fill_value=0)
    t["total"] = t.sum(axis=1)
    t["feedbacks"] = rows.groupby("topic")["ID"].nunique()
    t["net_sentiment"] = (t["Likes"] - t[["Difficult to Use", "Defect", "Wants"]].sum(axis=1)) / t["total"]
    t["pain"] = t[["Difficult to Use", "Defect"]].sum(axis=1)
    return t[t["total"] >= min_rows].sort_values("total", ascending=False)


topics = topic_table(cl)

top = topics.head(25)[FEEDBACK_TYPES].iloc[::-1]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 9))
left = np.zeros(len(top))
for ft in FEEDBACK_TYPES:
    ax.barh([short(i, 50) for i in top.index], top[ft], left=left, color=TYPE_COLORS[ft], label=ft,
            height=0.7, edgecolor="white", linewidth=1)
    left += top[ft].values
for y, v in enumerate(left):
    ax.text(v, y, f" {v:,.0f}", va="center", fontsize=8, color=INK_2)
ax.set_title("Top 25 topics by classified rows, split by feedback type")
ax.legend(ncol=4, loc="lower right")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
plt.show()
""")

code(r"""
views = {
    "Most liked (Likes)": topics.sort_values("Likes", ascending=False)["Likes"],
    "Biggest pain (DtU + Defect)": topics.sort_values("pain", ascending=False)["pain"],
    "Most wanted (Wants)": topics.sort_values("Wants", ascending=False)["Wants"],
}
side = pd.concat([pd.DataFrame({(k, "topic"): v.head(12).index, (k, "rows"): v.head(12).values})
                  for k, v in views.items()], axis=1)
side.index = range(1, 13)
side
""")

code(r"""
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 6.5))
t = topics[topics["total"] >= 20]
sizes = t["feedbacks"] / t["feedbacks"].max() * 600 + 20
sc = ax.scatter(t["total"], t["net_sentiment"], s=sizes, c=t["net_sentiment"], cmap="RdBu", vmin=-1, vmax=1,
                edgecolor="white", alpha=0.85)
ax.axhline(0, color=INK_2, linewidth=0.8)
ax.set_xscale("log")
for topic, r in t.iterrows():
    if r["total"] >= 45 or r["net_sentiment"] <= -0.6:
        ax.annotate(short(topic, 30), (r["total"], r["net_sentiment"]), fontsize=7, xytext=(5, 0),
                    textcoords="offset points", va="center")
ax.set_xlabel("classified rows (log scale)")
ax.set_ylabel("net sentiment")
ax.set_title("Volume vs sentiment per topic (≥ 20 rows): bottom-right = loud problems")
plt.show()

display(Markdown("**Most negative topics with ≥ 20 rows**"))
topics[topics["total"] >= 20].sort_values("net_sentiment").head(15)[FEEDBACK_TYPES + ["total", "net_sentiment"]] \
    .style.format({"net_sentiment": "{:+.2f}"}).background_gradient(subset="net_sentiment", cmap="RdBu", vmin=-1, vmax=1)
""")

md("### 3.1 What exactly do customers want? (level-3 nature of Wants and pain rows)")

code(r"""

# Domain = the most recent "Overall …" attribute; a few headers in the sheet don't start with "Overall".
DOMAIN_STARTS = {"Overall exterior styling": "Exterior", "Overall driving performance": "Driving performance",
                 "Overall power and pickup": "Power", "Overall interior styling/ aesthetics": "Interior styling & quality",

                 "Overall driver assist features": "Driver assistance",
                 "Overall driver-vehicle interaction (HMI)": "HMI & infotainment",
                 "Overall environmental friendliness": "Other"}

recs, attribute, domain = [], None, None
for _, row in raw_us.iterrows():

md(r"""

## 7. Triangulation: do the verbatims and the study agree?

Each requirement area is matched to its feedback topics (by keyword on the VFC topic name) and its study attributes
(by name). An area is **strong evidence** when both sources point the same way, and **conflicting** when one says
it's a problem and the other says it's fine. The mapping is hand-made and transparent. Edit `AREAS` to change it.
""")

code(r"""
AREAS = {
    # area: (regex on feedback topic, list of US study attributes)
    "Operating concept / HMI": (r"operating concept|touch ?screen|instrument cluster|body equipment, overall|operation",
                                ["Intuitiveness of controls", "Placement/ ease of reading and using controls",

    "Smartphone integration": (r"apple carplay|android|smartphone|bluetooth|wireless charg|phone",
                               ["Bluetooth/ smartphone pairing", "Mirroring of smartphone content on vehicle display",
                                "Place for phone", "Phone charging"]),
    "Connected services & app": (r"connecteddrive|app\b|my bmw|remote|digital key|wi-?fi|hotspot|navigation",
                                 ["Vehicle's Mobile App", "WiFi hotspot in vehicle", "If applicable: Navigation system"]),
    "Voice control": (r"voice|speech|intelligent personal assistant",
                      ["Performance of voice recognition"]),
    "Climate controls": (r"climat|heating|air condition|ventilat",
                         ["Operation of heater/ AC controls", "Overall performance of climate control system"]),
    "Seats & comfort": (r"seat|interior comfort",
                        ["Overall comfort of the seats", "Comfort of front seat", "Comfort of 2nd row seat",
                         "Driver seat adjustability"]),
    "Storage & cargo": (r"storage|luggage|trunk|stowage|cup ?holder",
                        ["Interior storage", "Cargo capacity/usefulness", "Ease of loading/unloading cargo",
                         "Trunk lid/ tailgate and liftgate operations", "Cupholders"]),
    "Range & charging (EV)": (r"electric range|charg(e|ing) high|public charging|charging|high-voltage",
                              ["Gas or electric mileage (fuel economy)", "Overall environmental friendliness"]),
    "Driver assistance": (r"assist|cruise control|parking|lane|camera",
                          ["Overall driver assist features", "Adaptive driving assists (lane keeping, cruise, braking)",
                           "Safety monitoring features (blid spot warning, lane departure warning, etc)"]),
    "Start-stop & drivetrain feel": (r"start-stop|msa|drivetrain|transmission",
                                     ["Overall power and pickup", "Smoothness of transmission", "Acceleration from stop"]),
    "Ride & handling": (r"handling|riding|driving dynamics|chassis|steering|braking",
                        ["Riding comfort", "Handling/Maneuverability", "Overall driving performance", "Braking"]),
    "Exterior design": (r"exterior design|^exterior$|lights?\b|wheel",
                        ["Overall exterior styling", "Headlight/ taillight design", "Appearance of tires/ wheels"]),
    "Interior design & ambience": (r"interior design|ambient|material|workmanship",
                                   ["Overall interior styling/ aesthetics", "Interior lighting",
                                    "Quality of interior materials", "Overall interior workmanship"]),
    "Audio": (r"audio|sound system|speaker",
              ["Overall performance of sound system", "Audio clarity", "Bass performance"]),
    "Noise & quality": (r"noise|rattl|squeak|vibration",
                        ["Overall noise/vibration/harshness", "Freedom from squeaks and rattles",
                         "Freedom from wind and road noise"]),
    "Value & ownership": (r"price|cost|warranty|service|dealer",
                          ["Overall value for money", "Affordable to buy", "Future trade-in or resale value",
                           "Economical to own (cost of ownership)"]),
}

all_topics = cl["topic"].unique()
bev_ids = set(feedbacks.loc[feedbacks.powertrain == "BEV", "ID"])
rows, topic_map = [], {}
for area, (pattern, attrs) in AREAS.items():
    tps = [t for t in all_topics if re.search(pattern, t, re.I)]
    topic_map[area] = tps
    r = cl[cl["topic"].isin(tps)]
    ids_pain = r[r.ftype.isin(["Difficult to Use", "Defect"])]["ID"].unique()
    ids_want = r[r.ftype == "Wants"]["ID"].unique()
    ids_like = r[r.ftype == "Likes"]["ID"].unique()
    attrs = [a for a in attrs if a in s60.index]
    sev = probs[probs["ID"].isin(r["ID"])]
    rows.append({
        "area": area,
        "topics matched": len(tps),
        "pain feedbacks": len(ids_pain),
        "wants feedbacks": len(ids_want),
        "likes feedbacks": len(ids_like),
        "net sentiment": (len(ids_like) - len(ids_pain) - len(ids_want)) / max(1, len(set(r["ID"]))),
        "BEV share of pain": np.mean([i in bev_ids for i in ids_pain]) if len(ids_pain) else np.nan,
        "serious C reports": int(sev["severity"].isin(["serious", "very serious"]).sum()),
        "study attrs": len(attrs),

    })
tri = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("area")

# Flag each source: is this area a problem according to it? Thresholds = median across areas.
fb_problem = tri["net sentiment"] < tri["net sentiment"].median()
st_problem = tri["study mean"] < tri["study mean"].median()
tri["agreement"] = np.select(
    [fb_problem & st_problem, ~fb_problem & ~st_problem, fb_problem & ~st_problem],
    ["both: weak", "both: strong", "feedback weak, study fine"], default="study weak, feedback fine")
tri.sort_values("net sentiment").style.format({
    "net sentiment": "{:+.2f}", "BEV share of pain": "{:.0%}", "study mean": "{:.2f}", "study bottom3": "{:.1%}",
    "top2 vs G70": "{:+.1%}"}).background_gradient(subset="net sentiment", cmap="RdBu", vmin=-1, vmax=1) \
    .background_gradient(subset="study mean", cmap="RdBu", vmin=4.8, vmax=5.8)
""")

colors = {"both: weak": "#e34948", "both: strong": "#1baf7a", "feedback weak, study fine": "#eda100",

# BMW 5 Series (G60) · United States — focus analysis

The hackathon asks for **one derivative in one market**. This notebook takes the 5 Series sedan (G60) in the US and goes
through all the BMW data for it. Each section ends with a short set of findings. The last sections combine everything
into an evidence table that can feed the requirements app.

| Dataset | File in `data/` | US 5 Series slice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sales volumes | `sales_volumes.xlsx` (sheet `G60_G68`) | US units 2024, 2025, 2030 (2030 presumably a plan) |

| Customer study | `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx` (sheet `US_2025`) | 103 attributes rated on a 7-point scale; the G70 column is used as a benchmark |

**Caveats that shape every number below** (details in `docs/datasets/`):

- Sales have **no powertrain split**, and the G60 sheet also counts the G68 (long wheelbase), which is sold in China, not the US.
- Feedback files hold **one row per classification**. Feedback counts use unique `ID`s, and topic counts use rows.

# Domain = the most recent "Overall …" attribute; a few headers in the sheet don't start with "Overall".
DOMAIN_STARTS = {"Overall exterior styling": "Exterior", "Overall driving performance": "Driving performance",
                 "Overall power and pickup": "Power", "Overall interior styling/ aesthetics": "Interior styling & quality",

                 "Overall driver assist features": "Driver assistance",
                 "Overall driver-vehicle interaction (HMI)": "HMI & infotainment",
                 "Overall environmental friendliness": "Other"}

recs, attribute, domain = [], None, None
for _, row in raw_us.iterrows():

md(r"""

## 7. Triangulation: do the verbatims and the study agree?

Each requirement area is matched to its feedback topics (by keyword on the VFC topic name) and its study attributes
(by name). An area is **strong evidence** when both sources point the same way, and **conflicting** when one says
it's a problem and the other says it's fine. The mapping is hand-made and transparent. Edit `AREAS` to change it.
""")

code(r"""
AREAS = {
    # area: (regex on feedback topic, list of US study attributes)
    "Operating concept / HMI": (r"operating concept|touch ?screen|instrument cluster|body equipment, overall|operation",
                                ["Intuitiveness of controls", "Placement/ ease of reading and using controls",

    "Smartphone integration": (r"apple carplay|android|smartphone|bluetooth|wireless charg|phone",
                               ["Bluetooth/ smartphone pairing", "Mirroring of smartphone content on vehicle display",
                                "Place for phone", "Phone charging"]),
    "Connected services & app": (r"connecteddrive|app\b|my bmw|remote|digital key|wi-?fi|hotspot|navigation",
                                 ["Vehicle's Mobile App", "WiFi hotspot in vehicle", "If applicable: Navigation system"]),
    "Voice control": (r"voice|speech|intelligent personal assistant",
                      ["Performance of voice recognition"]),
    "Climate controls": (r"climat|heating|air condition|ventilat",
                         ["Operation of heater/ AC controls", "Overall performance of climate control system"]),
    "Seats & comfort": (r"seat|interior comfort",
                        ["Overall comfort of the seats", "Comfort of front seat", "Comfort of 2nd row seat",
                         "Driver seat adjustability"]),
    "Storage & cargo": (r"storage|luggage|trunk|stowage|cup ?holder",
                        ["Interior storage", "Cargo capacity/usefulness", "Ease of loading/unloading cargo",
                         "Trunk lid/ tailgate and liftgate operations", "Cupholders"]),
    "Range & charging (EV)": (r"electric range|charg(e|ing) high|public charging|charging|high-voltage",
                              ["Gas or electric mileage (fuel economy)", "Overall environmental friendliness"]),
    "Driver assistance": (r"assist|cruise control|parking|lane|camera",
                          ["Overall driver assist features", "Adaptive driving assists (lane keeping, cruise, braking)",
                           "Safety monitoring features (blid spot warning, lane departure warning, etc)"]),
    "Start-stop & drivetrain feel": (r"start-stop|msa|drivetrain|transmission",
                                     ["Overall power and pickup", "Smoothness of transmission", "Acceleration from stop"]),
    "Ride & handling": (r"handling|riding|driving dynamics|chassis|steering|braking",
                        ["Riding comfort", "Handling/Maneuverability", "Overall driving performance", "Braking"]),
    "Exterior design": (r"exterior design|^exterior$|lights?\b|wheel",
                        ["Overall exterior styling", "Headlight/ taillight design", "Appearance of tires/ wheels"]),
    "Interior design & ambience": (r"interior design|ambient|material|workmanship",
                                   ["Overall interior styling/ aesthetics", "Interior lighting",
                                    "Quality of interior materials", "Overall interior workmanship"]),
    "Audio": (r"audio|sound system|speaker",
              ["Overall performance of sound system", "Audio clarity", "Bass performance"]),
    "Noise & quality": (r"noise|rattl|squeak|vibration",
                        ["Overall noise/vibration/harshness", "Freedom from squeaks and rattles",
                         "Freedom from wind and road noise"]),
    "Value & ownership": (r"price|cost|warranty|service|dealer",
                          ["Overall value for money", "Affordable to buy", "Future trade-in or resale value",
                           "Economical to own (cost of ownership)"]),
}

all_topics = cl["topic"].unique()
bev_ids = set(feedbacks.loc[feedbacks.powertrain == "BEV", "ID"])
rows, topic_map = [], {}
for area, (pattern, attrs) in AREAS.items():
    tps = [t for t in all_topics if re.search(pattern, t, re.I)]
    topic_map[area] = tps
    r = cl[cl["topic"].isin(tps)]
    ids_pain = r[r.ftype.isin(["Difficult to Use", "Defect"])]["ID"].unique()
    ids_want = r[r.ftype == "Wants"]["ID"].unique()
    ids_like = r[r.ftype == "Likes"]["ID"].unique()
    attrs = [a for a in attrs if a in s60.index]
    sev = probs[probs["ID"].isin(r["ID"])]
    rows.append({
        "area": area,
        "topics matched": len(tps),
        "pain feedbacks": len(ids_pain),
        "wants feedbacks": len(ids_want),
        "likes feedbacks": len(ids_like),
        "net sentiment": (len(ids_like) - len(ids_pain) - len(ids_want)) / max(1, len(set(r["ID"]))),
        "BEV share of pain": np.mean([i in bev_ids for i in ids_pain]) if len(ids_pain) else np.nan,
        "serious C reports": int(sev["severity"].isin(["serious", "very serious"]).sum()),
        "study attrs": len(attrs),

    })
tri = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("area")

# Flag each source: is this area a problem according to it? Thresholds = median across areas.
fb_problem = tri["net sentiment"] < tri["net sentiment"].median()
st_problem = tri["study mean"] < tri["study mean"].median()
tri["agreement"] = np.select(
    [fb_problem & st_problem, ~fb_problem & ~st_problem, fb_problem & ~st_problem],
    ["both: weak", "both: strong", "feedback weak, study fine"], default="study weak, feedback fine")
tri.sort_values("net sentiment").style.format({
    "net sentiment": "{:+.2f}", "BEV share of pain": "{:.0%}", "study mean": "{:.2f}", "study bottom3": "{:.1%}",
    "top2 vs G70": "{:+.1%}"}).background_gradient(subset="net sentiment", cmap="RdBu", vmin=-1, vmax=1) \
    .background_gradient(subset="study mean", cmap="RdBu", vmin=4.8, vmax=5.8)
""")

colors = {"both: weak": "#e34948", "both: strong": "#1baf7a", "feedback weak, study fine": "#eda100",

# BMW 5 Series (G60) · United States — focus analysis

The hackathon asks for **one derivative in one market**. This notebook takes the 5 Series sedan (G60) in the US and goes
through all the BMW data for it. Each section ends with a short set of findings. The last sections combine everything
into an evidence table that can feed the requirements app.

| Dataset | File in `data/` | US 5 Series slice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sales volumes | `sales_volumes.xlsx` (sheet `G60_G68`) | US units 2024, 2025, 2030 (2030 presumably a plan) |
| Customer verbatims | `G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` | `Country == "US"`: 3,610 unique feedbacks from Sources A–D |
| Customer study | `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx` (sheet `US_2025`) | 103 attributes rated on a 7-point scale; the G70 column is used as a benchmark |

**Caveats that shape every number below** (details in `docs/datasets/`):

- Sales have **no powertrain split**, and the G60 sheet also counts the G68 (long wheelbase), which is sold in China, not the US.
- Feedback files hold **one row per classification**. Feedback counts use unique `ID`s, and topic counts use rows.
- The feedback is **not a random sample of buyers**. Source B (dealer/call-centre paraphrases) is 73 % of it, and the
  powertrain mix of feedback is not the sales mix.
- The US study gives **shares per scale point but no sample size**, so we cannot test significance.

Run from the repository root or from `notebooks/`. The raw files must be in `data/` (they are not in git).
""")

code(r"""
STUDY = DATA / "F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx"
US_SCALE = ["I Hate It", "A Failure", "Unsatisfactory", "Satisfactory", "Excellent", "Delightful", "I Love It"]
raw_us = pd.read_excel(STUDY, sheet_name="US_2025", header=None)

# Domain = the most recent "Overall …" attribute; a few headers in the sheet don't start with "Overall".
DOMAIN_STARTS = {"Overall exterior styling": "Exterior", "Overall driving performance": "Driving performance",
                 "Overall power and pickup": "Power", "Overall interior styling/ aesthetics": "Interior styling & quality",
                 "Overall comfort of the seats": "Seats", "Overall interior design / layout": "Space & practicality",
                 "Overall performance of climate control system": "Climate", "Overall performance of sound system": "Audio",
                 "Placement/ ease of reading and using controls": "Controls",
                 "Overall noise/vibration/harshness": "NVH & sound",
                 "Overall impression of durability/reliability": "Reliability", "Overall safety of the vehicle": "Safety",
                 "Warranty coverage": "Value & ownership", "Overall brand image": "Brand",
                 "Overall driver assist features": "Driver assistance",
                 "Overall driver-vehicle interaction (HMI)": "HMI & infotainment",
                 "Overall environmental friendliness": "Other"}

recs, attribute, domain = [], None, None
for _, row in raw_us.iterrows():
    if pd.isna(row.iloc[0]):
        continue
    label = str(row.iloc[0]).strip()
    if label in US_SCALE:
        for col, code in {2: "G60", 3: "G70"}.items():
            recs.append((domain, attribute, code, label, float(row.iloc[col])))

        attribute = label
        domain = DOMAIN_STARTS.get(label, domain)
us_long = pd.DataFrame(recs, columns=["domain", "attribute", "series", "level", "share"])
dist = us_long.pivot_table(index=["domain", "attribute", "series"], columns="level", values="share", sort=False)[US_SCALE]

      f"{dist.sum(axis=1).min():.3f}–{dist.sum(axis=1).max():.3f}")
s60.groupby("domain", sort=False).size().to_frame("attributes").T
""")
